_meta.indication: Indicated in combination with a background immunosuppressive therapy regimen for the treatment of adult patients with active lupus nephritis (LN).

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 1:1 to LUPKYNIS 23.7 mg twice daily or placebo, each on background MMF and corticosteroids.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with SLE and ISN/RPS biopsy-proven active Class III or IV LN (alone or with Class V) or Class V LN; patients with baseline eGFR ≤ 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint: proportion of patients achieving complete renal response at Week 52 (UPCR ≤ 0.5 mg/mg and eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or no confirmed decrease from baseline in eGFR of >20%).
pivotal_trials.result: Complete renal response at Week 52: 40.8% (73/179) LUPKYNIS vs 22.5% (40/178) placebo; odds ratio 2.7 (95% CI 1.6, 4.3); p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥3%) include glomerular filtration rate decreased (26% vs 9% placebo), hypertension (19% vs 9%), diarrhea (19% vs 13%), headache (15% vs 8%), and anemia (12% vs 6%). Serious risks include nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity (including PRES), and hyperkalemia.
target_moa: Calcineurin-inhibitor immunosuppressant; voclosporin inhibits calcineurin in a concentration-dependent manner, blocking lymphocyte activation, with a supportive non-immunologic role in stabilizing podocytes in glomeruli.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: MALIGNANCIES AND SERIOUS INFECTIONS — increased risk for developing malignancies and serious infections with LUPKYNIS or other immunosuppressants that may lead to hospitalization or death.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was conducted for this application; the drug is not the first in its class and the application did not warrant discussion at an advisory committee meeting.

description.text: Updated labeling to include long-term efficacy and safety supporting use of Lupkynis (voclosporin) beyond one year
